items.text: Every adult should have an equal vote in choosing who governs, whatever their level of education or knowledge.
items.rationale: Universal equal franchise, sharpened against epistocracy; 'equal vote' (not 'say') avoids direct-democracy and wealth readings. Mirrors dem-02. Audit (draft 01): D 0.99.

items.text: The right to vote should depend on passing a basic test, the same for everyone, of how government works.
items.rationale: Epistocratic franchise as its defenders state it; 'same for everyone' blocks the discriminatory literacy-test reading. Mirrors dem-01. Audit (draft 09): H 0.97.

items.text: Any group of citizens should be free to form a party and run in elections to replace those in power.
items.rationale: Open political competition; 'any group' makes it strong. Cross-loads slightly on Liberty (militant democrats may hedge). Mirrors dem-04. Audit (draft 02): D 0.99.

items.text: One party or movement should lead the country for the long term, without rival parties competing for power.
items.rationale: Vanguardist / one-party view; persuasive 'clear vision' qualifier removed per review. Mirrors dem-03. Audit (draft 13): H 1.0.

items.text: If one party or family has held power for a long time, voters should have a fair chance to replace it.
items.rationale: Anti-entrenchment condition favours Democratic; rewritten from 'face real rivals' so dominant-party democracies read clearly. Mirrors dem-06. Audit (draft 05): D 0.99.

items.text: If elected lawmakers keep failing to solve serious problems, a single leader should be given power to act without their approval.
items.rationale: Strongman / executive-supremacy case from gridlock, the tradition the review found missing; condition favours Hierarchical. Cross-loads on Liberty (checks). New item, not blind-audited.

items.text: If voters and experts disagree about a major law, the voters' view should carry more weight.
items.rationale: Popular sovereignty over expertise, softened to a clear lean and mechanism-free so representative democrats can agree. Sole public-vs-expert item on this pole. Mirrors dem-08. Audit (draft 06): D 0.95.

items.text: If the public is deeply divided on a major question, a small council chosen for its wisdom, not by vote, should decide.
items.rationale: Council-of-the-wise view (Confucian, Platonic, clerical) without naming a faith; condition favours Hierarchical. Replaces technocracy duplicates 08/10. New item, not blind-audited.

items.text: Voters should be able to remove any elected leader before their term ends through a recall vote.
items.rationale: Strong contestability; the axis's only direct-democracy instrument (initiative item dropped to limit the direct-vs-representative conflation). Mirrors dem-10. Audit (draft 07): D 0.99.

items.text: The country should be led by a hereditary ruler who holds real power, not just a ceremonial role.
items.note: Hereditary: passed down within a family.
items.rationale: Sincere executive monarchism; 'real power' keeps constitutional monarchists on the Democratic side. 'The country' keeps it frame-sensitive. Mirrors dem-09. Audit (draft 12): H 1.0.

items.text: A good political system is one where bad laws and bad leaders can be replaced without violence.
items.rationale: I1 (institutions): Popper's criterion of democracy. Agreeing puts removability first, the Democratic pole; replaces the review's P0/P2. Wording approved by Max Kaye (project owner) for content v2, 2026-10-31; original.

items.text: To vote, serve on juries or hold office, people should first show they understand and accept the society's basic rules.
items.rationale: I5 (high civic standards): a conditional franchise is the Hierarchical pole (as dem-02), though here the test is acceptance of rules as well as knowledge. Wording approved by Max Kaye (project owner) for content v2, 2026-10-31; original.

items.text: When institutions make mistakes, being able to correct them quickly matters more than who chose the people in charge.
items.rationale: I6 (error correction over selection): ranks correction above the source of a mandate, so agreeing moves away from input (electoral) legitimacy toward the Hierarchical pole; populist and radical democrats disagree. Wording approved by Max Kaye (project owner) for content v2, 2026-10-31; original.

items.text: The most important question in politics is who should rule.
items.rationale: I7 (keyed against the institutions view): Plato's question. Doctrines of rule by the best (monarchy, vanguard, meritocracy) agree, so agreeing is the Hierarchical pole. Wording approved by Max Kaye (project owner) for content v2, 2026-10-31; original.

items.text: The head of state should be chosen by election, not by birth.
items.rationale: Separator for constitutional monarchism (its defining idea had no statement, review C4). Agreeing is the Democratic pole. Content v2 separator (CF review 2026-10-31 §5 draft, reworded); original.

items.text: If a law turns out to do more harm than good, citizens should be able to force a public vote to repeal it.
items.rationale: Citizen-initiated repeal: error correction by the public, the Democratic pole; balances dem-13. Content v2 separator (CF review 2026-10-31 §5 draft, reworded); original.
